headline: Revenue and earnings climb on higher volumes and price/mix
summary_short: Net sales rose 19.7% y/y to $4.00B and GAAP diluted EPS grew 9.2% to $0.83, as comparable operating earnings climbed 7.7% to $433M on higher global shipment volumes (+4.3%) and favorable price/mix.
summary_long: Revenue grew 19.7% y/y to $4.00B on higher volumes and favorable price/mix, mainly higher aluminum prices passed through to customers; global shipments rose 4.3%. Comparable operating earnings rose 7.7% to $433M, led by EMEA and South America, partly offset by higher North/Central America plant start-up and operating costs. GAAP net income rose 4.2% to $221M and diluted EPS rose 9.2% to $0.83 (comparable EPS $1.03, +14.4%); a $13M unrealized loss on equity-linked notes and higher business-consolidation charges tempered pretax income growth to 3.7%. Ball returned $222M to shareholders in H1 2026 and remains on track to return at least $800M for the full year, targeting 10-plus percent FY2026 comparable EPS growth and free cash flow above $900M.

drivers.explanation: CEO Ron Lewis attributed the quarter's higher volumes and operating earnings to the strength of customer partnerships and disciplined commercial and operational execution across Ball's global packaging portfolio.

All three segments cite higher shipment volume and favorable price/mix, primarily from higher aluminum prices passed through to customers; global aluminum packaging shipments rose 4.3% in the quarter.

The release explains comparable operating earnings (+7.7% to $433M): EMEA and South America gains from higher volume and price/mix more than offset higher plant start-up and operating costs in North/Central America.
Diluted EPS growth (+9.2%) outpaced net income growth (+4.2%) because weighted diluted shares fell 3.8% y/y on share buybacks.
The non-GAAP reconciliation shows a new $13M unrealized loss on equity-linked notes and $22M vs $12M higher business-consolidation charges partly offsetting the rise in comparable operating earnings.
The cash flow statement shows $115M of treasury stock acquisitions in H1 2026, consistent with the $222M of year-to-date shareholder capital returns cited in the highlights.

Gross profit (net sales less cost of sales excluding D&A) rose as the $659M increase in net sales outpaced the $610M rise in cost of sales, consistent with the volume and price/mix gains cited across all segments.
